newsitem.title: LATVIA: IMF sees few problems with new Latvia agreement.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees few problems with new Latvia agreement.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said on Thursday that it saw few problems in renewing a standby arrangement with the Baltic state of Latvia although it would like to see some more progress in structural reforms.
An IMF mission arrived on Wednesday in Latvia to renegotiate the standby, which comes up on August 23.
IMF Latvia and Estonia representative Dimitri Demekas said that the negotiations would focus on structural reforms such as tax administration, civil service reform and privatisation.
But he said the Fund was satisfied with Latvia's marcoeconomic performance.
"Based on their record so far, it should not be difficult to reach agreement," Demekas told Reuters.

The finance ministry said the mission would have talks with Finance Minister Robert Zile and officials from the ecomomy, welfare and agricultural ministries as well as the privatisation agency and state-owned utilities Latvian Gas and Latvenergo.
The ministry said in a statement that Latvia has had four standbys since 1992 and that of the first two it has used 51.22 million lats, of which approximately half has been repaid.
